en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 13.3.
Vipākattika (The Triplet on Resultant States)

Dependent on a resultant state as cause and object, a non-resultant state arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a resultant state, a state that is not of the nature to result arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a resultant state, a state that is neither resultant nor of the nature to result [arises]... by way of root-condition.

[An arisen state] arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a resultant state, both a state that is not of a nature to result and a state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to result arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a resultant state, both a state that is not resultant and a state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to result arise by way of root condition. (Five questions.)
Dependent on a state that is subject to ripening (*vipākadhammadhamma*), a state that is not subject to ripening arises by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is subject to ripening, a state that is not subject to ripening arises by way of the root-condition. Dependent on a state that is subject to ripening, a state that is neither subject to ripening nor subject to ripening arises by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is subject to ripening, both a state that is not subject to ripening and a state that is neither subject to ripening nor subject to ripening arise...
And states arise with a root condition. Dependent on a state that is subject to result, states that are neither results nor subject to result arise with a root condition. (Five questions.
Dependent on a state that is neither result nor subject to result, a state that is neither result nor subject to result arises.
By way of root condition: dependent on a state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to produce resultants, a state that is not a resultant arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to produce resultants, a state that is not of a nature to produce resultants arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to produce resultants, a state that is not of a nature to produce resultants and a state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to produce resultants [arise]... by way of root condition.

And states arise by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is neither-result-nor-state-predisposed-to-result, states that are both non-result and state-predisposed-to-result arise by way of root condition. (Five questions.
Dependent on a state that is both result and neither-result-nor-state-predisposed-to-result, a state that is non-result arises.
By way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is both resultant and neither-resultant-nor-producing-a-resultant, a state that does not produce a resultant arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is both resultant and neither-resultant-nor-producing-a-resultant, a state that is neither-resultant-nor-producing-a-resultant arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is both resultant and neither-resultant-nor-producing-a-resultant...
Dependent on a state that is not subject to result (navipākadhammadhamma),

there arise states that are both not subject to result and neither-result-nor-cause-of-result (nevavipākanavipākadhammadhamma) by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya). Dependent on a state that is both resultant (vipāka) and neither-result-nor-cause-of-result, there arise states that are not subject to result and neither-result-nor-cause-of-result by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is of the nature to ripen and a state that is neither fruition nor of the nature to ripen, a state that is not fruition arises by way of the root condition.

Dependent on a state that is of the nature to ripen and a state that is neither fruition nor of the nature to ripen, a state that is not of the nature to ripen arises by way of the root condition. Dependent on a state that is of the nature to ripen...
Dependent on a state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to result, states that are both neither resultant nor of a nature to result arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a resultant state, a state that is not of a nature to result arises by way of object condition... [three].

Dependent on a state that is of the nature to ripen (*vipākadhammadhamma*), a state that is not of the nature to ripen (*navipāka*) arises by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*) … three [questions].

Dependent on a state that is neither of the nature to ripen nor of the nature to have what ripens (*nevavipākanavipākadhammadhamma*), a state that is neither of the nature to ripen nor of the nature to have what ripens arises by way of object-condition … (five questions).

Dependent on a state that is both resultant (*vipāka*) and neither of the nature to ripen nor of the nature to have what ripens, a state that is not of the nature to ripen arises by way of object-condition … three [questions]. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to cause: twenty-three; with respect to object: fourteen; with respect to predominance: nineteen …pe… with respect to prenascence and repetition: nine …pe… with respect to result: five …pe… with respect to non-disappearance: twenty-three. (Abbreviated. With respect to not-cause: eighteen;
with respect to not-object: fifteen. With respect to not-predominance: twenty-three …pe… with respect to not-kamma:

six; with respect to not-result: eleven; with respect to not-nutriment, not-faculty: three; with respect to not-jhāna: six; with respect to not-path: fifteen …pe… with respect to not-dissociation: [fifteen].
Nine ... [and so on] ... fifteen non-disappearance conditions.
(The sections on co-nascence, condition, support, association, and conjunction should also be expanded in detail. 13.3.7.
Section on Questions (Pañhāvāra)

A resultant state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a non-resultant state. A resultant state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither resultant nor having the nature of being resultant.
A resultant state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither resultant nor having the nature of being resultant.

Condition: A resultant state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither-resultant-nor-possessing-the-nature-of-resultant and for a state that possesses-the-nature-of-resultant;
a resultant state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither-resultant and neither-possessing-the-nature-of-resultant.
A resultant state is a condition for a non-resultant state by way of object-condition. A resultant state is a condition for a state that is not of a nature to result by way of object-condition.
A resultant state is a condition for a state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to result by way of object-condition.
A resultant state is a condition for both a non-resultant state and a state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to result by way of object-condition.

It is a condition by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*). A resultant state (*vipāka-dhamma*) is a condition by way of object-condition for a state that is neither-resultant-nor-producing-resultant (*na-neva-vipāka-na-vipākadhamma-dhamma*), and for a state that is not-resultant (*na-vipāka*).
A resultant state is a condition by way of object-condition for a state that is neither-resultant-nor-producing-resultant and for a state that is not-resultant.
A state subject to ripening is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state not subject to ripening.

A state subject to ripening is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not ripening. A state subject to ripening is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither ripening nor subject to ripening.
A state subject to ripening is [a condition] for a state that is both not ripening and not subject to ripening...

And a state of the nature to produce result (vipākadhammadhamma) is a condition, by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya), for a state that is not of the nature to produce result (navipākadhammadhamma) and for a state that is neither resultant nor of the nature to produce result (nanevavipākanavipākadhammadhamma).
A state of the nature to produce result is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not resultant and for a state that is not of the nature to produce result.
A state of the nature to produce result is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not resultant and for a state that is not of the nature to produce result.
A state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to produce resultants is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither resultant nor of a nature to produce resultants … (six;

abbreviated). In the case of root-cause: thirteen; in the case of object: eighteen; in the case of predominance: seventeen; in the case of proximity: sixteen … (and so on) … in the case of conascence:

twenty-three; in the case of mutuality: thirteen; in the case of dependence: twenty-six; in the case of strong-dependence: eighteen; in the case of prenascence: six; in the case of postnascence: [six].
Nine in the case of repetition; six in the case of habituation; fourteen in the case of kamma; five in the case of result; thirteen in the case of nutriment; eighteen in the case of faculties;

thirteen in the case of jhāna; thirteen in the case of the path; nine in the case of association; ... [etc. ... twelve in the case of dissociation; ... [etc. ... twenty-six in the case of non-disappearance.
(The "Chapter of Questions" should be expanded in detail.)
